ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The magnetohydrodynamic generator is shown in the figure. Plasma is generated in the high-temperature combustion chamber and accelerated through the nozzle, entering the generation channel uniformly at a speed of $v=1000\mathrm{m/s}$. The generation channel has a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the paper, with a magnetic induction strength of $B=5\mathrm{T}$. The rectangular generation channel has a length of $a=50\mathrm{cm}$, a width of $b=20\mathrm{cm}$, and a height of $d=20\mathrm{cm}$. The resistivity of the plasma is $\rho=2\Omega\cdot\mathrm{m}$, and the internal resistance of the generator can be equivalent to a pure resistor. The external resistance is $R=16\Omega$.

1. Find the electromotive force $E$ and internal resistance $\boldsymbol{\mathrm{r}}$ of the generator.
2. Find the reading $I$ of the ideal ammeter.
3. Find the output power $\mathrm{P}_{out}$ of the generator.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows a magnetohydrodynamic generator. The high-speed plasma flows through the power channel to the right, indicated by arrows and the label v. The magnetic field region in the channel is marked with crosses, so B is directed into the plane of the paper. The vertical separation of the two collecting plates is marked d, and the external circuit contains an ideal ammeter A and an external resistor R. Reasoning: Since the plasma velocity is along the channel and the magnetic field is into the page, the motional charge separation occurs between the upper and lower plates, whose separation is d. Convert the dimensions: a = 50 cm = 0.50 m, b = 20 cm = 0.20 m, d = 20 cm = 0.20 m. The generator emf is E = Bvd = 5 × 1000 × 0.20 = 1000 V. The plasma between the electrodes acts as the internal resistance. Its current path length is d and its cross-sectional area is a b, so r = ρd/(ab) = 2 × 0.20/(0.50 × 0.20) = 4 Ω. The ideal ammeter is in series with the external resistance and internal resistance, so I = E/(R + r) = 1000/(16 + 4) = 50 A. The output power is the power delivered to the external resistor: P_out = I²R = 50² × 16 = 40000 W.
